description: This Bun.js module monitors tennis court availability from Club Automation's scheduling system and notifies users when desired time slots open up. It scrapes an internal scheduling endpoint that lacks proper authentication - anyone with knowledge of the endpoint and request parameters can access scheduling data.

text: The init function ensures a local user file exists and kicks off the monitoring loop. If users.json does not exist, it is created as an empty JSON file. Then checkCourts() fires immediately.

The checkCourts function runs on a 10-minute interval. It prevents overlapping executions with an isRunning flag. For each user, it iterates through active notifiers, disables expired ones, fetches court data for each relevant date, and calls timeChecker to evaluate available slots.
Court schedules come back as 15-minute intervals. The timeChecker merges consecutive intervals into contiguous availability blocks with from and to timestamps.
Each notifier specifies a desired court, start/end time, and minimum duration. The timeChecker evaluates whether any availability block satisfies those conditions before triggering a notification.

The getCourts function sends a POST request to the scheduling endpoint. The response HTML is parsed with Cheerio to extract enabled court slots from td elements. Each slot is converted into an object containing the formatted time and Unix timestamp.
The scheduling endpoint lacks authentication. Anyone using this script should comply with the service's terms of use and avoid exposing credentials or user data in logs or notifications.
